variants.note: own massing_affinities: massed-picturesque canonical (Cragside, Grim's Dyke), cross-gable-victorian canonical (Bedford Park). defining_characteristics #4: 'steep tile roofs with tall, thin, multiple chimney stacks.'

own massing_affinities: four-over-four 'possible: the smaller Queen Anne rectory or dower house, symmetrical and hipped, quoting the 1700 house directly' -- a real but secondary case, not the family's dominant picturesque massing.

CASCADE-PROVENANCE FIX. Wrongly resolved from english-palladian as the canonical form ('the roof is never the composed feature... kept behind a parapet') -- this is the WRONG hip roof: an invisible, parapet-concealed Palladian roof contradicts this style's own steep, visible, chimney-topped tile roof (already correctly bound at the family level in roof_pitch/chimney). The narrower 'quoted symmetrical dower house' hip case is real (see permitted, above) but is a visible tiled hip roof, not a Palladian one hidden behind a balustrade.

roof_form.rule: The dominant, canonical roof is a steep, visible, multi-gabled tile roof carrying tall chimney stacks as a primary silhouette element; a hipped roof survives only as the deliberate small-scale quotation of a genuine 1700 house, and even then is a visible tiled roof, never one concealed behind a classical parapet.

variants.note: defining_characteristics #4: 'steep tile roofs.' typical_ratios: 'Roof pitch 45-55 degrees in plain clay tile.'
CASCADE-PROVENANCE FIX. Wrongly resolved from mediterranean-vernacular -- a Mediterranean half-round barrel tile with no place in this style, which names plain clay tile explicitly.

roof_material.rule: Plain clay roofing tile, 45-55 degrees, and (in country 'Old English' work) tile-hanging on the upper storey wall as well as the roof.

brick_color.note: Hard co-occurrence constraint c01: brick 'must be red, finely jointed... breaking the red-and-white pairing removes the style's primary identity.'

primary_cladding.rule_append: Brick must specifically be RED (hard constraint c01), finely jointed, with cut and rubbed brick ornament at openings -- this is stricter than the inherited Georgian Flemish-bond binding, which does not fix a colour.
primary_cladding.rule: The inherited Georgian brick-Flemish-bond binding describes the bond correctly but is silent on colour; this style's own hard constraint (c01) makes red specifically non-negotiable, paired always with white-painted joinery.

variants.note: defining_characteristics #6: 'tile-hanging on upper storeys, half-timbered gables.' Hard structural constraint c03: 'Where tile-hanging occurs it must begin at a floor level and be carried on a proper oversailing course, never start mid-storey.'

secondary_cladding.rule: Tile-hanging (often fishscale or club-patterned) over the upper storey, beginning exactly at a floor line on a real oversailing course -- a construction event, not a decorative one (hard constraint c03).

parapet.rule: CASCADE-PROVENANCE FIX. Wrongly resolved from english-baroque as a classical balustraded parapet concealing the roof with urns and statuary. Wrong on two counts: the family's own order/column/entablature bindings already forbid true classical apparatus ('applied Victorian ornament copied flat onto a wall, never a real order'), and this style's own roof is a visible, chimney-topped tile roof (roof_form, above), never one concealed behind a parapet. Where a balustrade occurs in this style it is white-painted joinery on a porch or balcony (see `balustrade`), not a stone roofline parapet.

variants.note: own bay_rhythm: 'Irregular by intent. Windows are grouped in twos and threes where rooms need them, with wide blank brick between groups... a frontal symmetry, where it occurs, is local rather than overall.'

CASCADE-PROVENANCE FIX. Wrongly resolved from english-classical -- a rule stated to hold 'without exception... across every register of the family,' which is a rule about the CLASSICAL family and directly contradicts this style's own bay_rhythm text quoted above.

window_grouping_rule.rule: Windows group in twos and threes by room, separated by wide blank brick; alignment is local to a group, not a whole-facade grid.

variants.note: defining_characteristics #5: 'oriels, bays, balconies and recessed porches.' Exemplar Old Swan House: 'Three tall oriels on the first floor over a recessed ground storey.'
CASCADE-PROVENANCE FIX. Wrongly resolved from english-palladian -- a licensed classical exotic window with no place in a style whose classical-apparatus slots are family-forbidden.

special_window.rule: The special opening is the projecting oriel or bay window, not a classical Venetian or Diocletian window.

variants.note: No historical precedent. Treated as one more informal, picturesquely massed volume -- tile-hung or brick, gabled -- consistent with the style's own plan-driven, asymmetrical logic, never centred on the composed front.

garage_strategy.rule: INVENTED, no historical precedent. An informal gabled outbuilding, in the same red-brick-and-tile-hanging vocabulary as the house.

variants.note: defining_characteristics #4: 'Shaped, scrolled or pedimented Dutch gables.' A gable-top device, from the dutch-urban-gable-house hybridization (own lineage, weight 0.4), not a portico or doorcase pediment.

CASCADE-PROVENANCE FIX. Wrongly resolved from antique-classical+english-palladian as a rigorously proportioned Palladian centrepiece pediment 'landing on the rusticated basement.' This style has no rusticated basement and no such formal system -- its pediment is a gable-top scroll/curve quoted from the Dutch gable, applied Victorian ornament, not part of a proportioned classical order.

pediment.rule: Where a pediment occurs it caps a shaped or scrolled Dutch-derived gable, applied as domestic ornament -- not the base of a proportioned classical portico.

variants.note: defining_characteristics #1: 'Red brick, finely jointed, with rubbed and cut brick ornament -- aprons, panels, pilasters, sunflower and swag reliefs.' Applied surface relief, not a load-bearing member.

CASCADE-PROVENANCE FIX. Wrongly resolved from english-palladian as a fully proportioned window-aedicule pilaster under hard constraint c03 -- this style's own pilasters are flat cut-brick relief ornament, not a proportioned classical order member.

pilaster.rule: The pilaster appears only as flat, cut and rubbed brick relief -- one more piece of applied ornament alongside the sunflower and swag panels, never a proportioned classical member.

variants.note: defining_characteristics #2: 'White-painted joinery throughout: sashes, balconies, balustrades, porches and eaves.' A porch and balcony rail, in the white-against-red-brick pairing hard constraint c01 requires.

CASCADE-PROVENANCE FIX. Wrongly resolved from english-palladian as a stone parapet balustrade concealing the roofline -- see `parapet`: this style's roof is never concealed, and its balustrades are white-painted timber joinery on porches and balconies, not a masonry roofline device.

balustrade.rule: A white-painted timber balustrade on porches and balconies -- part of the red-brick/white-joinery pairing hard constraint c01 makes non-negotiable -- never a stone parapet concealing the roof.

ornament_vocabulary.rule: CASCADE-PROVENANCE FIX (family left this slot open for this exact member; the cascade below it wrongly supplied a classical 'licensed-points-only' rule). Corrected to this style's own documented vocabulary: cut and rubbed brick sunflowers, swags and pilaster panels (the sunflower being 'practically the movement's trademark'), plus terracotta enrichment after the 1862 International Exhibition's Japanese-detail influence -- diagnostic_tells, defining_characteristics.

ground_storey_m.note: SOURCE UNIT NOTE: own typical_ratios states this in metres (3.0-3.6 m); recorded as the numeric value despite the ft unit field, since no ft-denominated source figure exists and no metric unit exists in the schema's enum.

ceiling_height_rule.rule: CASCADE-PROVENANCE FIX. Wrongly resolved as a Palladian arithmetic/geometric/harmonic-mean derivation checkable 'against a published plate' -- directly contradicted by this style's own governing_logic: 'No applied system. Composition is picturesque and plan-driven, with proportion controlled locally.' Storey heights are 'much less graduated than Georgian, since the composition no longer depends on it' (own typical_ratios) -- rooms vary in size and ceiling height as their USE requires (description.long), not as a plan-ratio formula dictates.

variants.note: description.long: 'inglenooks, window seats, and stairs that turn around a landing with a window on it.' Rooms 'vary in size and ceiling height as their use requires.'

CASCADE-PROVENANCE FIX. Wrongly resolved from english-georgian -- a heavy formal classical profile family inconsistent with this style's own described informality and its family-level rejection of a true classical order.

trim_family.rule: A lighter, informal domestic trim register -- inglenooks, window seats, turned stair landings -- consistent with the style's own described cheerfulness and comfort rather than a graded classical entablature system.
trim_family.note: EDITORIAL: specific trim profile dimensions are not itemized in this node's own text; the correction is grounded directly in its described interior character.

variants.note: defining_characteristics #5: 'Picturesque asymmetrical composition generated by an informally planned interior, with oriels, bays, balconies and recessed porches.'
CASCADE-PROVENANCE FIX. Wrongly resolved from english-classical, which explicitly forbids the very informal/irregular partis this style's own defining_characteristics describe directly.

circulation_parti.rule: The plan is informally arranged first, with rooms of irregular size and shape as use requires; the elevation -- oriels, bays, gables -- is the plan's consequence, not a governing classical hall-and-stair figure.

variants.note: defining_characteristics #7: 'Abundant daylight and a deliberate cheerfulness of colour and detail, in explicit contrast to High Victorian Gothic.' description.long: 'the light is abundant and the view is uninterrupted at eye level.'
CASCADE-PROVENANCE FIX. Wrongly resolved from mediterranean-vernacular's 5-20% aperture-to-wall thermal-mass figure -- the opposite of this style's own explicitly stated abundant daylight.

daylight_strategy.rule: Generous, large-paned windows -- clear glass below the small-paned upper sash -- are a deliberate design principle, in direct, stated contrast to Gothic Revival's darker interiors.

variants.note: description.long: Bedford Park, begun 1875, 'modest brick houses with tile-hung gables, white-painted balconies and existing trees preserved between them. It is the first garden suburb, the direct ancestor of Hampstead, Letchworth and every leafy suburb in the English-speaking world.'

landscape_idiom.rule: The house sits informally in a leafy setting with mature trees preserved rather than cleared -- the garden-suburb model this style itself originated at Bedford Park (1875).
